svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', 'Noto Sans', Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: What each layer can catch, and why the misses happen
svg.desc: A grid. Four things that can leak out of a repository are set against the four layers that might stop them: the pre-commit hook and the pre-push hook, which run with rules you wrote; GitHub push protection, which runs with GitHub's rules; and publishable check, a command-line tool you run yourself that checks a git repository for things you would not want public. A green dot means the layer stops it, with the rules named under each column heading. A red ring means it gets through, with the reason written underneath. An AWS or Stripe key is stopped by all four. A home path or an internal host or an agent's working note gets past GitHub push protection, because push protection has no pattern for them. The same path, already sitting in an older commit, gets past the pre-commit hook and, after your first push, the pre-push hook too, because it is outside the change they are handed, and past push protection for the pattern reason. publishable check is the only column that stops all four, and a final row asks whether each layer runs without you, answered in words rather than marks: the hooks run on every commit or push, and publishable check runs only when you remember. A note records that on a very first push pre-push is handed the whole history and does catch that bottom row, and that a repository you are about to make public has already been pushed, so it is past that case. The closing argument: nothing here runs at the moment you make the repository public, since that is a settings change rather than a push, so you run publishable check yourself beforehand, and it covers that moment rather than replacing the hooks. Every column, publishable check included, only finds what someone wrote a pattern for, and nothing here catches a fact nobody described. Against the hooks publishable check wins one row and it wins it on reach rather than intelligence, and against push protection it wins three rows, all three for the single reason that push protection only knows key formats.
svg.text: publishable is a command-line tool that checks a git repository for things you would not want public.
Filled green: it ships with the rule. Hollow green: only if you wrote that rule. Red: it gets through, reason below.
these three run on their own
this one you run by hand

g.text: your home path, or an internal host
you deleted the file, the commit stayed
Why that cell says after your first push: a first push has no remote branch to compare against, so pre-push is handed everything.
A repository you are about to publish is long past that.

svg.text: Nothing here runs at the moment you make the repository public. That is a settings change, not a push.
Run it last, in the repository, just before you flip it to public.
check is a subcommand of publishable.

g.text: Every column here, publishable check included, only finds what someone wrote a pattern for.
Nothing here catches a fact nobody described.
Against the hooks: count a hollow green as a loss and it wins all four; count it as a win and it wins the already-committed row alone.
Against push protection it wins three rows, all three for the same reason: push protection only knows key formats.
